documents.title: H&P - Admission - COPD Exacerbation
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 03:40, HD1
CC: Worsening shortness of breath x 3 days
HPI:
69 yo male with known COPD (GOLD 3) presents via EMS at 01:25 with 3 days of progressive dyspnea, wheeze, and productive cough.
Sputum changed from clear to yellow-green 2 days ago. No fevers reported at home. No chest pain, no orthopnea, no leg swelling.
Used home albuterol MDI q2h without relief the day prior to arrival. Ran out of tiotropium about 10 days ago.
SpO2 89% at triage; 1L NC started, SpO2 92%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Denies hemoptysis, sick contacts, recent travel, or aspiration event.
PMH:
COPD, 2 prior admissions for exacerbation
Former smoker, 50 pack-years, quit 4 years ago
Hypertension
Hyperlipidemia
Chronic rhinitis
Remote appendectomy
Home meds:
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily (out of supply)
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Allergies: penicillin - rash
Social: lives with wife in one-story home. Daughter nearby. No alcohol. No illicits.
FHx: father with emphysema, mother with CAD
ROS: positive for dyspnea, cough, wheeze, fatigue. Negative for fever, chills, nausea, dysuria, rash.
Exam:
Gen: ill-appearing, sitting forward on edge of bed, anxious
HEENT: mucous membranes dry, no JVD
Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze both fields, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur
Abd: soft, nontender, nondistended
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no asterixis
Skin: warm, dry
Labs/Studies:
WBC 12.4, Hgb 14.6, Plt 244
Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 101, HCO3 29, BUN 16, Cr 0.94, glucose 118
Troponin 0.02, BNP 62
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or effusion
ECG: sinus tachycardia at 106, no acute ischemic changes
Resp viral panel sent
Assessment/Plan:
69 yo male with acute COPD exacerbation, likely infectious trigger, with hypoxemia and increased work of breathing. No evidence of pneumonia, HF, or ACS.
1. COPD exacerbation: continue albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h scheduled and q2h prn; systemic steroid per below; doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 5 days given penicillin allergy and purulent sputum.
2. Hypoxemia: O2 by NC, titrate to SpO2 90-94%. Wean as tolerated.
3. Monitoring: telemetry overnight, RN respiratory checks q2h, RT at bedside for neb administration and education.
4. HTN: hold lisinopril tonight given borderline volume status, resume in AM.
5. Tachycardia: expect improvement with beta-agonist washout and improved gas exchange; recheck HR after nebs.
6. Glucose monitoring q6h while on systemic steroids.
7. Prophylaxis: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
8. Diet: heart healthy. Activity as tolerated with assist.
Discussed plan with pt and wife at bedside. Pt able to nod and give short answers. Admit to telemetry unit.
Disposition: admit, expect short stay if work of breathing improves.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
S: Pt reports breathing much improved overnight. Slept about 5 hours sitting up. Cough now looser, sputum lighter in color. Able to speak in full sentences this morning.
Overnight: RN notes no desaturations below 90%. One prn neb at 23:40, none since.
O:
T 36.9, HR 88, BP 132/78, RR 18, SpO2 94% on room air after wean at 06:00
Gen: comfortable, sitting upright in chair, no tripod posture
Lungs: mild scattered expiratory wheeze upper fields, air movement improved, no crackles
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
Abd: soft, nontender
Ext: no edema
Labs: WBC 9.8, Na 139, K 4.0, Cr 0.90
Resp viral panel negative
A/P:
COPD exacerbation - clear improvement. Work of breathing resolved, off supplemental O2 since 06:00.
Steroid: transition from IV to oral. Oral steroid: prednisone 40 mg by mouth daily, tolerated without hyperglycemia.
Continue albuterol-ipratropium neb q6h, spacer teaching by RT this morning.
Continue doxycycline 100 mg PO BID, day 2 of 5.
Resume lisinopril 20 mg PO daily.
Ambulate in hallway with RN, document SpO2 with exertion.
Discontinue telemetry if no arrhythmia by midday.
If ambulatory saturations hold above 90% on room air, anticipate discharge later today.
Plan discussed with pt; wife to be updated by phone.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 14:45
Interval: Ambulated 300 ft in hallway at 11:30 with RN. SpO2 93-95% on room air throughout, HR peak 96, no dyspnea requiring stop.
Pt requested regular diet, ate full lunch without difficulty.
RT completed inhaler technique teaching at 12:10; pt demonstrated correct MDI with spacer, 2 of 3 attempts on first pass then correct after coaching.
O:
Gen: sitting in chair, conversational, no distress
Lungs: minimal end-expiratory wheeze at right upper field only, otherwise clear, good air movement
CV: RRR
Ext: no edema
Glucose 124 at 12:00
Telemetry discontinued at 13:00, no arrhythmias recorded.
A/P:
1. COPD exacerbation - resolved to baseline function. Off oxygen >8 hours, ambulatory sats stable.
2. Continue prednisone 40 mg PO daily to complete 5 day course; no hyperglycemia noted on q6h checks.
3. Continue doxycycline to complete 5 day course.
4. Restart tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily - new supply arranged before departure.
5. Continue budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID; albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn.
6. Smoking: remains abstinent 4 years, reinforced.
7. Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination status reviewed with RN, influenza vaccine given at 14:00.
Disposition: stable for discharge home this afternoon with wife. Follow-up in pulmonary clinic in 1 to 2 weeks, primary care in 1 week.
Discharge instructions and return precautions reviewed with pt and wife at bedside 14:30.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1 03:40, discharged HD2 16:10. Length of stay 2 days.
Discharge diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of COPD with acute hypoxemic respiratory distress, likely infectious trigger
Secondary: COPD GOLD 3, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, former smoker 50 pack-years
Hospital Course:
69 yo male presented with 3 days of progressive dyspnea, wheeze, and purulent sputum.
SpO2 89% at triage; 1L NC started, SpO2 92%.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
CXR showed hyperinflation without consolidation. ECG sinus tachycardia, troponin 0.02, BNP 62. WBC 12.4 on admission, 9.8 on HD2. Resp viral panel negative.
Admitted to telemetry. Treated with scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers, systemic steroids, and doxycycline 100 mg PO BID.
Work of breathing improved steadily overnight HD1. Supplemental oxygen weaned off at 06:00 on HD2.
Oral steroid: prednisone 40 mg by mouth daily, tolerated without hyperglycemia. Glucose checks q6h ranged 106 to 124.
Ambulated 300 ft on HD2 with SpO2 93-95% on room air, HR peak 96. Telemetry discontinued 13:00 with no arrhythmias.
Lisinopril resumed HD2 morning. Inhaler technique with spacer taught by RT and demonstrated back correctly.
Discharge exam: T 36.8, HR 84, BP 128/74, RR 16, SpO2 94% room air. Minimal wheeze right upper field, good air movement, no distress.
Discharge Medications:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily to complete 5 day total course (3 days remaining)
Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID to complete 5 day total course (3 days remaining)
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 2 puffs BID, rinse mouth after use
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn with spacer
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Follow-up:
Primary care in 1 week for post-hospital visit and BP check
Pulmonary clinic in 1 to 2 weeks for spirometry and inhaler review
Return Precautions:
Return or call if dyspnea at rest, inability to speak full sentences, chest pain, fever above 38.3, confusion, or no relief from rescue inhaler.
Pt and wife verbalized understanding of medications, taper completion, and return precautions.
Discharged home ambulatory with wife at 16:10.
